articles.author: lyric0x10
articles.description:
The Challenge: Protecting Python Source Code


I’ve been building a custom obfuscator that goes beyond simple variable renaming by transforming code into a virtualized and encrypted state using AST manipulation.
I wanted to share a quick "Before and After" to show how dramatic the transformation is.
Here is a standard Python script. It's clean, readable, and easy to reverse-engineer.
print("Hello world")

x = 10
y = x + 5
z = (y * 2) - x 

print("Result:", z)


Using a custom engine, I put the code through several layers of protection:
AST Minification & Variable Renaming


String Encryption & Number Mangling

Control Flow Flattening
Virtualization (VM Generation)
The logic is now running inside a custom virtual machine layer. You can see the full obfuscated output in the Gist below:
While no obfuscation is 100% unbreakable, virtualization makes reverse engineering significantly more difficult and time-consuming.
What do you think? Is the performance hit worth the extra layer of protection, or is this just a lot of work for 'security through obscurity'?
articles.title: Python Obfuscation: From Readable to Untraceable

articles.description:
Why I Built Staks: Open-Source Email Infrastructure for Developers
I'm launching, Staks, an open-source email infrastructure platform built specifically for developers in emerging markets.
The Problem
Email infrastructure is broken for developers outside the US.
Sendgrid charges $300k+/year for enterprise plans. Mailgun costs $90/month for 100,000 emails. For developers in India, Brazil, Nigeria, and other emerging markets, this is simply not affordable.
I've been there. I've watched talented developers build amazing products but struggle to send transactional emails (password resets, order confirmations, etc.) because the infrastructure costs are prohibitive.
The Solution: Staks
$50/month for UNLIMITED emails.
No per-email charges. No surprises. No hidden fees.
Key Features:
99.9% uptime SLA- Your emails get delivered
Simple REST API- Integrate in minutes
Email templates- Pre-built templates for common use cases
Real-time analytics- Track opens, clicks, deliveries
Open-source - Self-host or use managed
Developer-first - Built by developers, for developers
Why Open-Source?
Transparency matters. Developers want to know how their email is being sent. With Staks, you can:
Audit the code
Self-host if you want
Contribute improvements
Build on top of it
The Market
There are 500,000+ developers in emerging markets who need affordable email infrastructure. They're building SaaS products, e-commerce platforms, and fintech apps. They deserve infrastructure that doesn't cost a fortune.
We're in Beta
I'm looking for early users to help shape Staks. If you're interested:
Sign up for beta:https://staks.dev

Check out the code: https://github.com/edbarki77-arch/Staks-core

Share feedback: Reply in the comments
What's Next?
Week 1: Validation (getting early users)
Week 2-3: MVP (building the core product)
Week 4: Beta launch (first paying customers)
I'll be documenting the entire journey here on Dev.to. Follow me for updates!
Questions? Ask in the comments below!
articles.title: Why I Built Staks: Open-Source Email Infrastructure for Developers
